payload.description:
## Trigger

When my beads file is over 4 MiB, I want the work items read with no setup and fast, so I can use handily on projects with 10k beads.

## Evidence

The engine's $.fs.read rejects a file over 4 MiB and $.process.run keeps only the first 4194304 bytes; $.process.spawn streams with no cap (mods/handily-workitems/.claude-plugin/types/claude-code/index.d.ts:3227 and 3517). Today a file over 4 MiB runs br list after approval. The approval exists for programs a repo can influence (docs/design.md rows 10, E, F); a fixed system reader on a fixed path is not one.

## Design

Stream .beads/issues.jsonl through $.process.spawn: <redacted:posix-absolute-path> on Linux and macOS, cmd.exe /d /c type from System32 on Windows, by absolute path; refuse a reader that resolves inside the repo root. Parse each line as it arrives; skip closed and tombstone lines with a text check before JSON.parse; keep only open items; yield between chunks; read again only when size or mtime changes. Dolt stays as it is.

## Scope

mods/handily-workitems readers, snapshot and tests; README and docs/design.md beads rows; changelog fragment.

## Confirmation Plan

claude plugin test mods/handily-workitems; npm run check; a generated 10k-bead file of about 30 MB timed on WSL and on Windows against br list.

## Trigger

When a session polls an unchanged tracker every 2 seconds, I want the poll to cost almost nothing, so I can keep a large beads project open all day.

## Evidence

Measured on Claude Code 2.1.299, WSL, with a probe mod that times await $.workitems.refresh() (handily-fwkt.2.4 comments, 2026-10-14). On an unchanged signature, readOnce in mods/handily-workitems/hooks/snapshot.ts publishes the whole snapshot again only to update checkedAt, and detect, the config read and the stat add about 15 $ calls.

## Scope

mods/handily-workitems snapshot and poll, its tests, and each consumer of checkedAt if its place changes.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a mod test runs close to its time limit on a developer machine, I want the local gate to refuse it before the push, so I can fix it before a slower CI runner turns the gate red for no defect.

## Evidence

handily-fwkt.8.24: a handily-board test took 4445 ms of its 5000 ms limit on a green CI run, then 5436 and 5964 ms on two red runs (basicly-gates 38633439999 and 38634676960). Locally it took about 2100 ms then, so the local gate saw nothing. claude plugin test prints each test with its time, for example '(pass) name [2056.38ms]', and a test limit is 5000 ms unless its TestOptions set timeoutMs (types index.d.ts lines 16620-16628).

## Design

scripts/mods.mjs reads the per-test times that claude plugin test prints and fails the test step when a test used more than a set share of its limit. The share and how the script learns a test's own limit (the default, or a declared timeoutMs) are open; the threshold comes from measured local and CI times, so a slow developer machine does not flag tests that pass on CI.

## Scope

scripts/mods.mjs test step, scripts/mods.test.mjs, CONTRIBUTING.md.

- When the session starts, task-pane shall register the model tools `task_add`, `task_update` and `task_list` through $.tool.register, and add a system prompt section that tells the model to keep its plan in them.

- When the session has no tasks, the pane and /task shall list the tracker open items with explicit add buttons and add nothing on their own; an item already a task shall not be added twice.
- When the person runs /task pane, the pane shall open; userConfig mode off, toggle or always shall set the default.
- The list shall reset on session.end with reason clear, and survive a hot reload.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When a reply holds a handover, a plan or a table, I want to copy the whole block with one click or one key, so I can paste it into a chat, an email or another agent.

## Evidence

- Button and $.ui.copy (types index.d.ts:1053-1076, 2531-2544). A Button hotkey works only in the plugin's band or pane, never the composer (1070-1076).
- $.ui.selection sees nothing with fullscreen off (2553-2554).

## Trigger

When a session runs many subagents with long task lists, I want the board to redraw without a visible delay, so I can keep it open all day.

## Evidence

handily-board keeps the lists of at most 100 agents and 100 tasks each (mods/handily-board/hooks/tasks.ts lines 53-55). No test or measurement shows how a draw scales with the number of agents. A pinned time in a test would depend on the machine and break the rule that tests stay deterministic, so the time is measured live and the test pins the work per draw instead. Method from handily-fwkt.2.5: a probe mod timed engine calls in a live session with $.clock.now().

## Scope

handily-board this session and this machine tabs: a deterministic test of the engine calls per draw, a live timing with 30 agents of 20 tasks, a fix where the work grows with the agents, README.

## Trigger

When I use devloop in a repository, I want the test lock hook installed only after I allow it, never over an existing hook manager, so I can trust that a plugin never changes my git hooks silently.

## Evidence

- Claude Code has no plugin install, update or enable hook event; SessionStart can install on first use; bin/ is on the Bash PATH; npm dependencies install from a lockfile; CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA survives updates (code.claude.com docs, read 2026-10-08 by the docs specialist).
- handily design: mods show and ask, never enforce (docs/design.md:16-21).

## Scope

- A scratch plugin and scratch repos in the session scratchpad. No repo file changes.

## Confirmation Plan

A builder agent writes the scratch plugin and a script; I run it live on tmux -L handily-live against three scratch repos: no hooks, pre-commit config, lefthook config.

payload.text: Result 2026-10-08, Claude Code 2.1.295, scratch plugin hook-probe on tmux -L handily-live. (1) A repo with .pre-commit-config.yaml: no question, a refusal that names the manager, no hook written. (2) Inside a mod, git config --get core.hooksPath returns <redacted:posix-absolute-path> although the shell returns nothing: Claude Code disables hooks for the git commands a mod runs. So a mod must not read core.hooksPath or --git-path hooks/pre-commit through its own git calls; read .git/config or use --git-common-dir. With <redacted:posix-absolute-path> ignored the ask appeared once (Not now default, Install for this repo). (3) git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit gave no usable path inside the mod, so the install failed; the probe still kept the answer install and does not retry: the real mod must keep the answer only after the install works, or reinstall when the hook file is missing. (4) The builder ran the hook in a clone: an unrelated commit passed, a change or delete of an approved test was refused with the file named. (5) Install routes, measured by the builder: npm lefthook 2.2.1 runs from node_modules/.bin with no global install, but its postinstall runs lefthook install in INIT_CWD, so install with --ignore-scripts; uvx pre-commit 4.6.2 needs uv and a uv-managed Python, and uvx pre-commit install writes a uv cache Python path into the hook, which a cache clean breaks. (6) API gaps: $.fs.write has no file mode (chmod needs $.process.run), $.fs has no delete, AskOptions has no default (the first option acts as it), $.plugin has no data folder. Verdict: a plugin can install a test lock with consent; a plain hook script with no hook manager is the most robust route.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When Claude calls any tool, built-in or MCP, I want simple-view to draw it as one short row, so I can stop asking which tools the mod supports.

## Evidence

On 2026-10-14 simple-view shortens a fixed list: Bash, Edit and Write (mods/handily-simple-view/hooks/register.ts line 35 and lines 347-349) and Read, Grep and Glob (hooks/reading.ts line 3). Every other tool draws the engine's full row: about 70 other built-in tools in the 2.1.300 tool table, such as WebFetch, WebSearch, Agent, NotebookEdit, Skill and ToolSearch, and every MCP tool. A native Linux build registers no Grep or Glob, and a Windows build has its own shell tool, so a fixed list also misses tools per platform. Every tool call has a name, an input and a result, so one generic row can draw any tool.

## Design

A generic row for any tool: the tool name (an MCP tool as server and tool), a short summary of the input, the state (running, done, error), and the result size or time. The 6 current rows stay as richer rows on top. Tools that ask the person or show a plan keep the engine row: an exclusion list that starts on the safe side (AskUserQuestion, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, and any tool whose result the person must read to answer). A row that another mod already draws (handily-board task tools, quiet-items tracker writes) stays that mod's row. /simple show N prints any call in full.

## Scope

mods/handily-simple-view: the generic row, the exclusion list, the hand-off to other mods, tests on terminal and desktop, a live check, README, docs/guide.md, docs/design.md section 4.8, changelog fragment.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: When a subagent has a task list, its card shows the tasks in list order, each with a mark: done, in progress or open, and a count of done tasks. When the list has more than 5 tasks, the card shows the task in progress, the 2 tasks before it and the 2 after it, and the count. When the person focuses a card and presses Enter, the card unfolds to the whole list, and Enter again folds it. When the subagent has no list, the card draws as today. A done card shows the last real tool, not SubagentHandback (handily-yxfev).

- When a subagent has a task list, its card shows the tasks in list order, each with a mark for done, in progress or open, and a count of done tasks.
- When the list has more than 5 tasks, the card shows the task in progress, the 2 tasks before it, the 2 tasks after it, and the count.
- When the person focuses a card and presses Enter, the card unfolds to the whole list, and Enter again folds it.
- When the subagent has no list, or task-pane is not installed, the card draws as before.
- docs/mocks.md section 5 shows a card with a plan, and npm run check passes.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When subagents keep a plan, I want each agent-board card to show that agent's tasks in order with done, in-progress and open marks, so I can see how far each agent is without asking.

## Evidence

- task-pane keeps one list per agent at task-pane/agentList keyed by the agent id, indexed by task-pane/agentIds (mods/task-pane/types/index.d.ts, merged in 1b887de and e752a90).
- session-board reads task-pane state with a local type and no plugin dependency (mods/session-board/hooks/progress.ts:3, register.tsx:27,167); agent-board does the same, so it still loads without task-pane.
- The card layout is in docs/mocks.md section 5.

## Scope

- mods/agent-board/hooks/*
- mods/agent-board/*.test.ts*
- mods/agent-board/README.md
- mods/agent-board/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
- docs/mocks.md

## Confirmation Plan

claude plugin test mods/agent-board and npm run check; the main session runs a live check on tmux -L handily-live with two subagents that keep a list.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When a reply holds a markdown table, the mod draws it without box lines, with aligned columns.
- When the screen is narrower than 40 columns or a column would get fewer than 6 cells, each row draws as a block: the first cell in bold, then one label colon value line for each other column.
- When the person presses copy on a table, the clipboard holds the table as markdown; when the person presses copy as text, it holds label colon value lines.
- When the person presses copy on a fenced block, the clipboard holds the block content without the fences.
- When a fenced block has a tag, the mod draws a title line that names the tag.
- When the person runs /replies, the view turns off or on for the session.
